verdict.rationale: Intuit's official MCP server exposes environment variables (QUICKBOOKS_DISABLE_WRITE, QUICKBOOKS_DISABLE_UPDATE) and lets you restrict which tool categories are registered, and the OAuth client supports a sandbox/production split—giving some coarse-grained, least-privilege-style control over what an agent can do. However this is app-level config rather than true per-agent scoped OAuth credentials/roles, and there's no documented fine-grained scope system (e.g., read-only vs specific entity scopes) issued per credential. Missing for 10: granular OAuth scope definitions, role-based API key issuance per agent, and independent confirmation these toggles are enforced server-side rather than just client config.
